summary.headline: The Select Board voted on revised Special Town Meeting warrant articles, supporting two-family zoning and irrigation but voting against trails funding.
summary.summary: At a brief special meeting, the Select Board reopened and reclosed the warrant for the October 17, 2026 Special Town Meeting to consider revised language for three articles. The board voted unanimously to support revised Article 2 regarding two-family zoning and revised Article 3 for Community Preservation Act irrigation funding, but voted 1-4 against supporting revised Article 4 for CPA trails funding. The board also postponed discussion of town financial procurement policies to October 6 and made two temporary appointments to the Cultural Arts Council.

topics.title: Special Town Meeting warrant articles 2, 3, and 4
topics.summary: The board reopened the warrant for the October 17, 2026 Special Town Meeting to act on updated article language submitted after consultations between town boards and town counsel. Members unanimously supported revised Article 2 (two-family zoning changes recommended by the Zoning Board of Appeals and Planning Board) and Article 3 (CPA-funded irrigation). The board voted 1-4 against supporting Article 4 (CPA-funded trails), maintaining its previous opposition despite clean-up edits.
key_details: Special Town Meeting is scheduled for October 17, 2026.
Article 2 amends two-family zoning regulations with adjustments requested by the Planning Board.
Article 3 and Article 4 are Community Preservation Committee proposals for irrigation and trail projects.
The board voted 5-0 to reopen the warrant and later 5-0 to reclose it.
Article 4 failed to win Select Board support by a 1-4 vote, with only one member in favor.
topics.outcome: Articles 2 and 3 supported; Article 4 opposed; warrant reclosed.
topics.why_it_matters: These articles will go before voters at the October 17 Special Town Meeting with the Select Board's formal recommendations recorded in the warrant.

topics.title: Financial procurement policy update
topics.summary: The board considered updated language in the draft financial policies regarding procurement and confidentiality, reviewed by town counsel to align with public records law exemptions. A board member raised questions regarding the statutory language under Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 30B Section 6 on opening RFP price proposals. The board agreed to postpone review and adoption of the policy to its October 6 meeting to allow more review time.
key_details: Town counsel Liz Lydon reviewed confidentiality language and replaced previous draft non-disclosure agreement terms with public records exemption standards.
Questions were raised regarding procedures for handling price proposals during RFP evaluations under Chapter 30B.
A related matter involving a recommendation from the Conservation Commission to reduce unauthorized debt for Breakneck Hill was also deferred to October 6.
topics.outcome: Discussion deferred to the October 6 meeting.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved the re-appointment of two former members to the Southborough Cultural Arts Council to ensure a quorum so the council can distribute state grants.
key_details: Jane Gates was appointed for a term ending in 2027.
Jane Lesniewski was appointed for a term ending in 2028.
Additional appointments to the Cultural Arts Council are scheduled for October 6.
